passages.title: Task 1
passages.text:
(1) Every spring, when the ice on the river in Ganaa's town melts, it reveals a whole winter of rubbish: plastic bottles, bags, old tyres and broken toys. For years, people living nearby simply complained about it. Then, five years ago, a group of university students decided to do something more useful than complain.

(2) Their leader, a biology student named Ganaa, explains how it started. "We were walking by the river one weekend and counted more than two hundred bottles in less than a kilometre," he says. "We realised that if we waited for someone else to clean it, we would wait forever."

(3) The students began by meeting every Saturday morning with gloves and sacks. They posted photos online of the riverbank before and after each clean-up. Soon schoolchildren, families and even local businesses were asking to join, and the group now has more than six hundred members.

(4) The volunteers do not only collect rubbish; they also record what they find. Their notes show that the amount of plastic has fallen steadily since they started, especially near the parks where they have put up signs and extra bins. Fewer bottles are now left on the banks, and people seem more careful.

(5) Ganaa admits that cleaning a river is a job without an end. However, he believes the real success lies in people's attitudes. "Nobody who has spent a morning picking up other people's rubbish ever throws a bottle on the ground again," he says with a smile.
